learning_outcomes.text: Students recognize fundamental structures of their already familiar practice of ethical argumentation and are also aware of the central conflicts of interest in economic arrangements.
Students develop a deeper understanding of the inescapability of value judgments in theory and practice. They know fundamental approaches for justifying trade-offs.

Students become aware of the fact that professional responsibility exists and it is not possible to remain neutral about it. They can classify competing business ethical approaches and recognize their relevance for their own positioning.
Students can make ethically reflected and well-founded decisions in the face of conflicts of interest in professional life.

Students identify ethically challenging situations in professional life. They can assess when a monological evaluation is no longer appropriate and how, in such cases, the necessary knowledge gain and normative understanding can be achieved by involving other actors.

Students can identify conflicts of interest in professional situations and explain them in a differentiated manner. They can knowledgeably justify the systematic importance of ethical requirements for economic actors and their practical implications.
Students recognize the unavoidability of professional responsibility and the inherent demand in professional action (as social action) to be able to comprehensively justify actions.

syllabus_topics: The inescapability of value judgments in theory and practice
Objectives of companies and their legitimization
Limits of the "Business Case for Business Ethics"
Entrepreneurial success in the service of social development
Artificial Intelligence and responsibility: Data-based discrimination
Planned obsolescence ("predetermined breaking points" for sales promotion)
Dealing with employees between profit interest and moral claims
Asbestos, Contergan & Co.: Technology assessment, major risks and the precautionary principle
Vision, Mission and Code of Ethics
assessment_rules: The portfolio examination is worth 100 points and consists of two written assignments (AP) and a one-hour exam (K1). Each AP can yield a maximum of 30 points, and K1 can yield a maximum of 40 points. Alternatively, K2 may be chosen at the discretion of the examiner. The duration of the exam within the portfolio examination and the written assignment within the portfolio examination (approx. 3-5 pages each) are as per the valid study regulations.
